channel.title: Oncolopedia
channel.description: News, explainers and frequently asked questions about cancer, without the jargon.

item.title: HIV and cancer: what has changed since the first cases of Kaposi sarcoma
item.description: 1 December is World AIDS Day. AIDS was discovered partly through a rare cancer, Kaposi sarcoma. Today HIV treatment has reshaped the map of cancer in people living with HIV.

item.title: What Europe recommended in November: new medicines for lung, prostate and kidney cancer
item.description: The European Medicines Agency's medicines committee backed two new lung cancer drugs and new uses in prostate and kidney cancer. What it means, and what it does not.

item.title: Welcome to Oncolopedia
item.description: A free oncology encyclopedia, in English and Spanish, with official sources on every page. What you will find and what you won't.

item.title: Marie Curie, our cover photo
item.description: Why we chose Marie Curie to open Oncolopedia, and what the discovery of radium has to do with today's treatments.

item.title: Cancer in numbers: what the latest global data say
item.description: About 20 million new cases and 9.7 million deaths a year. Which cancers are most common, what has changed and what can be prevented.
